newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases on dlr, market jittery.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases on dlr, market jittery.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened marginally on Monday on increased dollar demand from foreign investors, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling rate of 53.45 against the dollar from 53.43 on Friday, while against the pound it was posted at a mean rate of 87.21 from 87.26.
Dealers said foreign investors opted to pull out of the market after making unsuccessful bids at last week's treasury bill auction.
"A lot of them were quoting above 20 percent even after we advised them that rates were going down," one dealer said.
Last Thursday's T-bills auction offered an average yield of 19.677 percent on the main 91-day category of bills, down from 19.904 in the previous auction.
"The market is jittery. We began at 53.30/55 but we're now doing 53.45/75 and we think in some places it could be as high as 53.60/80," one dealer said.
"What is coming in (dollars) is not enough to sway the market. We have big buying orders from offshore investors," another dealer said.
The money market continued liquid with overnight quoted at 9 percent compared to 7-10 percent on Friday.
